title: AD Forest Health Assessment and Recovery-Readiness Capstone
summary: Combine replication diagnostics, FSMO awareness, Kerberos delegation review, gMSA hygiene, and forest-recovery planning into one enterprise health assessment and remediation plan.
scenario: You are the newly assigned senior AD engineer for a three-domain forest (root + two child domains, 14 DCs total) that has had no dedicated AD owner for the past year. Leadership wants a health assessment and a prioritized remediation plan before the next audit cycle.
business_context: The organization is mid-acquisition-integration; a second company's domain is expected to establish a forest trust within 6 months, raising the stakes on delegation hygiene and FSMO/replication health specifically.
technical_constraints: No forest-wide maintenance window longer than 4 hours is available for the next quarter; any FSMO role changes must be graceful transfers, not seizures, since all current holders are believed reachable; the organization's only tested backups are 45 days old.
functional_requirements: Produce a replication health map across all 14 DCs identifying any DC with a failure age approaching the tombstone lifetime.
Produce a current FSMO role-holder inventory with a documented standby holder recommendation per role.
Identify any unconstrained Kerberos delegation grants forest-wide and classify each as remediate-now vs migrate-planned.
Audit all gMSA/sMSA usage for privileged-group membership and authorization-list hygiene.
Produce a forest-recovery readiness gap list (e.g. backup currency vs the 45-day findings, untested plan, DSRM password currency) with a remediation timeline.
non_functional_requirements: The assessment itself must not require any forest-wide outage.
All proposed remediations must respect the 4-hour maintenance window constraint.
Findings must be presentable to both a technical infra team and a non-technical leadership audience.
architecture_decisions: Run replication and FSMO inventory checks read-only, forest-wide, before proposing any change.
Treat the upcoming forest trust as the forcing function for prioritizing delegation and gMSA hygiene work ahead of other lower-urgency findings.
Schedule the first forest-recovery drill in an isolated lab (per OSB-AD-LAB-0003) rather than deferring it, given the 45-day-old backup finding raises real recovery-point risk today.
implementation_plan: Week 1: forest-wide read-only assessment (replication, FSMO inventory, delegation scan, gMSA audit) - no changes made yet.
Week 2: remediate low-risk, high-value findings within maintenance windows (graceful FSMO transfers to documented standbys, orphaned SPN/gMSA authorization cleanup).
Week 3: address any DC approaching tombstone-lifetime replication failure per OSB-AD-TS-0001's decision tree.
Week 4: run the isolated-lab forest recovery drill (OSB-AD-LAB-0003) and update the recovery plan with real findings from the drill, not just the paper plan.
Ongoing: institute the monitoring thresholds and group-based gMSA authorization patterns from OSB-AD-TS-0001 and the gMSA lab as standing practice ahead of the forest trust go-live.
risk: The pending forest trust means any unresolved unconstrained-delegation or replication-health issue becomes a shared risk with the acquired company's domain the moment the trust is established - this is called out explicitly as the reason delegation/replication findings are prioritized ahead of less time-sensitive items.
security: Unconstrained delegation findings and gMSA privileged-group memberships are treated as security findings, not just operational hygiene, and are reported to the security team in parallel with the infra remediation plan.
operations: All remediation steps are scoped to fit inside the stated 4-hour maintenance windows; anything that can't (e.g. a full DC rebuild under OSB-AD-TS-0001) is scheduled as its own dedicated window rather than forced into the standard cadence.
cost: No new licensing or infrastructure spend is required for this capstone's scope - the work is entirely configuration, process, and one isolated lab VM for the recovery drill.
validation: Re-run the forest-wide replication and FSMO inventory checks after Week 3 to confirm 0 outstanding replication failures and that all FSMO holders match the documented standby plan; confirm the recovery drill's validation steps (OSB-AD-LAB-0003) pass before considering the recovery-readiness gap closed.
rollback_dr: Every remediation step in this plan (FSMO transfer, SPN/authorization cleanup, DC rebuild) has its own documented rollback in the underlying lesson/lab/troubleshooting record it's drawn from; the forest-recovery drill itself runs on a disposable isolated VM specifically so it carries no production rollback risk.

assessment_rubric.replication_assessment_complete: Every DC's replication status is accounted for with a specific classification (healthy / approaching risk / already exceeded tombstone lifetime), not a single forest-wide summary number.
assessment_rubric.fsmo_plan_quality: Standby holder is named per role with a stated rationale (connectivity, reliability), not just 'any other DC.'
assessment_rubric.delegation_findings_prioritized: Unconstrained delegation findings are explicitly ranked against the forest-trust timeline, not treated as a flat backlog.
assessment_rubric.recovery_readiness_realistic: The gap list names the actual 45-day backup finding and DSRM password currency as concrete items, not generic 'test the DR plan' language.
assessment_rubric.maintenance_window_respected: No proposed remediation step in the implementation plan exceeds the stated 4-hour window without being called out as its own dedicated window.
